sections.h2: Contacting the Marathon County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds works from the courthouse at 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403. Phone 715-261-1470; the fax line is 715-261-1488. Staff file deeds, land contracts, mortgages, satisfactions and assignments for property anywhere in the county.

Holiday weeks and closures shift the schedule, so phone ahead before carrying an original deed to the counter. Shortened days and one-day closures do come up, and the county posts them, so a quick call saves a wasted trip downtown. Have the parcel or the names on the deed ready when you call. Documents can also be mailed in, handy if you live elsewhere.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Marathon County
sections.html:
The 2020 count was 138,013 people, and July 2025 brought an estimate of 139,432 (up 1.0 percent). Housing units total 62,059, with 73.3 percent owner-occupied. Median value for an owner-occupied home is $219,600, median gross rent is $999 a month, and builders pulled 348 permits in 2025.

Whether the house is in Wausau or in Athens, Edgar, Marathon City, Mosinee, Rothschild, Spencer or Stratford, the deed is filed at one office on Forest Street.

Filing a real estate document costs $30, and the county adds $1.00 per filed document for certification. Copies of what's on record are $2 for the first page and $1 for each page after. Recorded documents sent by email are charged the same per-page rate. The state transfer fee is a separate charge, due when you hand in the deed.

ServiceCost
Recording a real estate document$30 per document
Certification$1.00 per filed document
Paper copies$2 first page, $1 each added page
Emailed copies$2 first page, $1 each added page
State transfer fee30 cents per $100 of value

Write the $30 check to Register of Deeds, and include any transfer fee with it.

The office has a short routine for property transfers. The county gives no legal advice. Take deed wording questions to an attorney or abstract company.

  1. Prepare the deed, notarized or authenticated. When it names specific parcels, include the full legal description.
  2. File the Wisconsin electronic transfer return with the state. The receipt shows up on the second screen after you submit, so print it.
  3. Enclose the $30 recording fee payable to Register of Deeds, with any transfer fee.
  4. Mail the packet to Register of Deeds, 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403.
  5. Put your email address on the paperwork. Since January 1, 2026, documents come back electronically unless you include a self-addressed, stamped envelope.

The deed must also show who drafted it, plus the name and mailing address of the person who gets it back. If all you have is an out-of-state form, a cover sheet can supply the title, return address and parcel number where the office wants them.

The standard layout comes from Wis. Stat. 59.43(2m), and a deed that departs from it can be turned away. The office lists these requirements:

  • Stamp area: an empty 3 by 3 inch square in the upper right of page one.
  • Name and return address: just below the stamp area, or along the left edge inside the top 3 inches.
  • Parcel identifier number: immediately below the return address.
  • Title: inside the top 3 inches but not in the stamp corner.
  • Paper and ink: ordinary white letter or legal sheets, black ink, so the scanner reads them.
  • Margins: half an inch above, a quarter inch elsewhere, on each page.
  • No hinged pages.

State law forbids recording anything that displays a person's Social Security number. Delete it before you mail.

Starting September 3, 2019, Marathon County switched to the Ascent Land Records Suite from Transcendent Technologies on September 3, 2019. Land and tax information is at ascent.co.marathon.wi.us/ascentlandrecords. The real estate index can also be searched free in LandShark, though viewing or printing a recorded document there costs a fee.

The county surveyor, at 715-261-6000, holds survey material. Online folders there cover benchmarks, section summaries, plats of survey and tie sheets, sorted by town and range. Before you sign a sale contract, look over the recorded chain of title and any survey so surprises turn up early.

Public records are presumed open. A denial has to come with specific reasons, and the person refused can sue to compel release. Surveys and the chain of title are the records sellers most often want, and both are worth pulling before a listing goes live so a buyer's title company finds nothing unexpected.

When the owner has died, the county's recording page has forms ready: Personal Representative Deed, Designation of TOD Beneficiary, Termination of Decedent's Interest (with instructions), Quit Claim Deed and Warrant Deed. Passing a house along by will, descent or survivorship carries no state transfer fee under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11), provided the deed states that reason.

A later sale by the heirs is its own conveyance. The seller owes the usual 30 cents per $100 of value there.

Most returned packets share a few causes. The transfer return receipt is missing, so print it the moment it appears on the second screen. The check is made out to the wrong payee instead of Register of Deeds, or it is short because the transfer fee was left off. The deed has no drafter named, or no name and mailing address for its return. A Social Security number is showing. Or the page layout puts the title inside the stamp corner. Go through the packet once against the layout list above before you seal the envelope. Because documents now come back electronically, a missing email address can also leave you waiting. Add one, and enclose a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you would rather have paper in hand.

Often the title company or closing attorney does the filing, and the seller never sets foot in Wausau. The sequence is still worth knowing. You sign the deed in front of a notary. The transfer return gets filed online and the receipt printed. Then the packet travels to Forest Street with $30 and whatever transfer fee is due. A cash purchase has no lender mortgage to record, which makes the stack thinner, yet the deed and return remain mandatory. After recording, the deed sits in the public index that later buyers and title searchers read. Filing it yourself? Phone 715-261-1470 beforehand and ask what the staff want to see.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Marathon office?
faqs.a: Call 715-261-1470, or fax 715-261-1488. The office is at 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403. Phone ahead for current hours, since temporary schedule changes happen.
Recording is $30 per document. Certification adds $1.00 per filed document, and copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page. Any state transfer fee is extra.

faqs.q: Can a deed go by mail?
faqs.a: Yes. Mail the deed, your printed return receipt, and a $30 check made out to Register of Deeds to 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403. Add any transfer fee and an email address, plus a stamped return envelope if you want paper back.

faqs.q: Do I owe the transfer fee on a sale?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Sellers owe 30 cents per $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22 unless an exemption fits, as it does for transfers by will, descent or survivorship.

faqs.q: Where do I search recorded documents?
faqs.a: Use LandShark for the free real estate index search, and the Ascent site at ascent.co.marathon.wi.us/ascentlandrecords for land and tax information. Viewing or printing a recorded document in LandShark costs a fee.
